title: Math Class
subtitle: Should we really be studying math at a time like this?

items.text: Math Class
The Hall of Apeiron
The classroom is as usual, with the same mathematics being taught.
And the same teacher.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: So, what exactly are you confused about?
Her confusion is evident.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Peace and love.
He mutters, his mind far away from the numbers on the board.
One of the Manus followers raises a hand.

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: Why can π be an infinite, non-repeating decimal and also represent a precise angle?

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: According to your logic, doesn't that violate the law of excluded middle?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Ah, a flawed argument.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: The premise for using the law of excluded middle is that the two concepts are mutually exclusive. But decimals and angles are not dichotomous concepts.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: A circle's angle follows its own rules, so it's reasonable that 180° equals π.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Still, the fact that you're attempting to use logic to solve these problems is a significant step forward!

items.speaker: Manus Follower II
items.text: I don't ... understand.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Hmm.
She reviews the steps in the reasoning.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: It's a clear explanation, rudimentary even. What is there not to understand?

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Yeah, isn't it clear enough already?
His outburst isn't particularly loud, but still draws the attention of the others.
The not-so-eloquent follower glances at him, then responds to 37's words.

items.speaker: Manus Follower II
items.text: I just ... don't understand ... anything.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Very well. I'll start again from the beginning.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Let's take another look at the problem. It asks us to calculate the area of the shadow!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: The area of a plane figure can be reduced to an accumulation of definite integrals.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: We can establish a system, set shadow area as S, then write out the formula.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: This is the most straightforward method!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: However, this solution does lose the elegance of geometry. Even though it's correct, I don't find it to be a good process.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Process …

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Yes, people won't believe an answer without a good process.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Just like how "peace and love," without actions to live up to the words, is just an empty slogan.
He admits it reluctantly.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: As for solving this problem ...
37's demonstration is interrupted by someone approaching through the stone-lined halls.

items.speaker: Island Believer I
items.text: 37, the leader is looking for you, for Apeiron's Trial.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: But I'm in the middle of …

items.speaker: Island Believer I
items.text: Don't worry. I'll take over teaching these irrational numbers.
After 37 leaves, her replacement immediately puts on a stern face—clearly, he is not fond of outsiders.
He glances around, then walks over to a corner and begins studying the scroll in his hand.

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: It seems like he has no intention of continuing the lesson.
The man whispers.

items.speaker: Manus Follower II
items.text: It's ... too hard.

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: It's just about circumference and radius.
He sketches the figure out on scrap paper and begins pondering over it.
She extends her pen and draws a large × over the figure. Then, she writes a message to him.

items.speaker: Manus Follower II
items.text: "Stop studying. Let's talk about our escape."

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: Oh, right!
He sets aside the figures and numbers.

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: "The question is how to escape? We know almost nothing about this island!"

items.speaker: Manus Follower II
items.text: "I discovered the route where 6 takes his walks. I planted a bomb there. Once it goes off, we can get out of this place."

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: "Where in the world did you get a bomb?"

items.speaker: Manus Follower II
items.text: "I made it."
The man shoots a skeptical look at her.
The sound of writing continues.

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: "Look, all I'm saying is you copy your homework from me, and making a bomb is way harder than trigonometry!"

items.speaker: Manus Follower II
items.text: "It just hasn't been triggered yet."
The man shakes his head.
The writing becomes more frantic.

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: "Instead of trusting in a bomb, here's a better idea. Let's jump the leader while he's out for a walk."

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: "Trust me. Before joining Manus, that was basically my main source of income."

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: "Besides, fate is clearly on our side. How else can you explain what happened to me this morning?"

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: "I found a Browning pistol on the beach."

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: No—

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: Quiet! You idiot!

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: That Browning is …

items.speaker: Island Believer I
items.text: Browning?
The island believer, who has been flipping through a scroll, looks up in surprise.

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: No, no, it's a type of dessert called a brownie.
The island believer approaches them and takes the scribbled note.
Then, a puzzled expression crosses his face.

items.speaker: Island Believer I
items.text: A bomb?
Living in seclusion, far from conflict, they have completely forgotten words associated with violence.

items.speaker: Island Believer I
items.text: And what are you planning to do while our leader is out for his walk?

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: I heard that 6 is a number representing balance.

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: So, uh …
He struggles to find something fitting to say about numbers, but his limited vocabulary fails him.

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: So, we want to go for a walk with him.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: According to your theory, 6 symbolizes harmony, and we happen to need more peace in our lives.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Still, maybe we should be concerned about the leader's mental health, too.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: People often walk to relieve stress. If someone is always walking around alone, it could be that there is something making them feel powerless.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Like an artist trying to learn mathematics.
The island believer gives him a knowing smile.

items.speaker: Island Believer I
items.text: Is that so?

items.speaker: Island Believer I
items.text: I'm curious, how have you discovered these insights into human nature without a proper mathematical foundation?

items.speaker: Island Believer I
items.text: Your spirit of exploration is commendable, but without the guidance of Truth, all exploration is fruitlessly cyclical.

items.speaker: Island Believer I
items.text: In order to help you better bask in the light of Truth,

items.speaker: Island Believer I
items.text: I believe we must extend today's math lesson.
A damp, dark cell.

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: If he's a number, he's definitely a really annoying one. I never want to study math again.

items.speaker: Manus Follower II
items.text: Me neither. My head ... hurts.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: I think the dream bubble isn't the solution to our problems. It might just be a fleeting fantasy.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: But, if we don't use the dream bubble, how can we show everyone that beautiful world?

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: I don't know what to do.
His musings catch the attention of his companions.

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: What are you talking about now?

items.speaker: Manus Follower I
items.text: Come up with any creative ideas for escaping this place?
He realizes something.
Perhaps "peace and love" would never convince these people. After all, that has never been the creed of Manus Vindictae.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: Hmm.
A flash of insight.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: We're forbidden from using arcane skills, and it's not appropriate to resort to violence.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: But when I was at the beach, I saw remnants of boats and geometric structures.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: It seems that, years ago, they attempted to leave.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: So, they can't be completely disengaged from the world.
He falls deep into thought.

items.speaker: Diggers
items.text: The first thing we need to do is disguise ourselves as the island's inhabitants to find a way out.
